claims.text:
diffusion-denoising

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:diffusion-denoising` → `ai-diffusion-denoising` → `src/demos/ai/ai-diffusion-denoising`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/80`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#3-diffusion-denoising`. **Packet:** G2. **Level / prerequisites:** core; `ai:gradient-descent`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** gradient-descent optimizes parameters; this computes forward corruption and an actual Bayes reverse process, with uncertainty rather than oracle recovery.

**Computed primary model:** Binary clean bitX0 priorP(1)=.5, two independent flip transitions probability.25 each. Enumerate all eight(X0,X1,X2) paths. ObserveX2=1: posteriorP(X1=1|X2=1)=.75; applying the correctly conditioned reverse process yieldsP(X0=1|X2=1)=.625. Retain the observed bit1 separately from the uncertain clean-bit distribution. No hidden clean-bit oracle enters reversal.

**Countercase / boundary:** Change priorP(X0=1) to.9, same noise and observation: posteriorP(X0=1|X2=1)=.9375, not.625. Reverse probabilities depend on prior and time. This is a binary diffusion analogue, not a Gaussian DDPM implementation or evidence that denoising reconstructs a unique original.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether observing noisy1 proves clean1; recall a single.25-flip step under balanced prior gives posterior.75, while two steps give.625.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Corrupt then Reverse one/two layers computes path masses, normalization and posterior bars; Change prior restarts current computation while retaining balanced-prior witness. Display conditional labels and bit uncertainty explicitly.

**Source obligation:** [Ho et al. original PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.11239), opened2026-10-19, §2 forward/reverse Markov definitions Eq1–2 as motivation. The finite binary conditional model is independently derived, not those Gaussian parameterizations or image results.
